title: China Trains 2026: a Standing Ticket Costs the Same as a Seat | China Travel Expert
description:
On a sold-out China bullet train, the last ticket left can be a standing one — for the same price as a seat.

China's high-speed trains sell a “no-seat” ticket (无座) once the seats are gone. It's officially the same seat class as second class, so 12306 charges the identical fare — no discount for standing. On a long run like Beijing–Shanghai (about 4.5 hours) that can mean standing most of the way. Why the two cost the same even trended on Chinese social media in August 2026.

🧭 Expert Tip: Before you pay on 12306 or Trip.com, check the seat type and skip anything marked “no-seat” (无座); if a train is sold out, try another departure or book 1–3 days ahead.

高铁票卖光后还能买到“无座”——价格和二等座一模一样。
